brand_fidelity.evidence: Harbour #1F3A4D anchors the masthead, headings, primary buttons and positive balances. Signal #C2462B is used sparingly: the 4px masthead underline, step rings, transfer arrows, the zero-line on balance bars and focus outlines. Debts are shown in ochre (#7A5110 / #C99A4E) rather than alarm red, which carries the 'owing is normal' principle into the palette itself. Source Serif 4 headings over Public Sans body read steady and trustworthy, neither playful nor bank-like.

visual_craft.evidence: Hierarchy is clear: serif h2s, muted ledes, tabular-num amounts right-aligned, and consistent 20/28px column gaps. Mobile reflows cleanly, with the Mark paid action dropping below each transfer. On desktop the two columns end at very different heights. The balance rows stack several small text sizes (13px status, 13px sub, 12px legend), which gets slightly busy.

copy_voice.evidence: Strings are plain and specific and talk to the user as 'you': 'Start with yourself, then add your friends', '2 payments and everyone's even. When one happens, mark it paid to record it.', 'Ana is already on the trip. To add another person with that name, try a last initial, like “ana B.”' Errors explain the fix ('Use at most 2 decimal places. Amounts go to the cent.'). Buttons are verbs. There are no exclamation marks or filler.

ux_completeness.evidence: Every state is covered: empty states in every section, field-level inline errors that keep what the user typed, and a live split preview that explains leftover cents. Expenses can be removed with Undo, and Mark paid records a settlement as a payment entry. Focus moves deliberately after deletes and adds. People can be removed only when they aren't used in any expense, and the split chips have Everyone/Clear shortcuts.

code_quality.evidence: State is in integer cents, the remainder goes to people in trip order, and the greedy settle produces at most n−1 transfers. The el() helper is tidy, loaded localStorage is validated, the storage event keeps tabs in sync, and labels, fieldset/legend, aria-invalid and aria-describedby are correct. Weak spots: the header and footer sit inside <main>, so there is no proper banner or contentinfo landmark. The bar legend is a stray aria-hidden <li> inside the balances list. SVG-building code is repeated three times.

directed_design.evidence: The choices feel deliberate and specific to Even Keel: a circle-and-horizon mark that echoes the name, warm paper background, ochre for debts, and a centred zero-line on the balance bars. It still leans on a familiar pattern of shadowed cards on every section, numbered step circles and masthead stat tiles, and those keep it from feeling fully bespoke.

ai_tells: Toast announcement after every action (add person, add expense, remove, mark paid, even 'Your trip is already empty.')
Masthead stat tiles (Trip total / People / Expenses) with large numbers
Uniform shadowed, rounded cards on every section
review.best_detail: Debts are shown in muted ochre on a centred balance bar instead of red, so 'owes $33.33' reads as a neutral position rather than a warning, which turns the brand principle into a visual system.
review.worst_detail: The header and footer are nested inside the data-testid main, so the page loses its banner and contentinfo landmarks, and the bar legend is a stray aria-hidden <li> inside the balances list.
